newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-RAI PLAYS DOWN BRAZILIAN INFLUENCE IN FINAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RAI PLAYS DOWN BRAZILIAN INFLUENCE IN FINAL.

text.p: Rai on Tuesday downplayed the presence of four Brazilians in Wednesday's European Cup Winners Cup Final.
Holders Paris St Germain will field Brazilians Leonardo and Rai against Barcelona's Ronaldo and possibly Giovanni in the final at the Feyenoord Stadium.

PSG are also coached by Brazilian Ricardo Gomes who said the match had aroused enormous interest in Brazil, one of 156 countries televising the game live. The estimated worldwide audience is put at 350 million people.
Ricardo told reporters on Tuesday: "A lot has been said about four Brazilians being in the final and although they will exert an influence in the match, they are not the only ones playing.

"I do not think it will just be a game of our Brazilians and their Brazilians looking to win a mini-battle between each other. Of course there will be a lot of pride and prestige at stake, but they are all part of our teams and not just individuals. That is the most important thing."
But Ronaldo is one player who could have the biggest impact on the game.
Still only 20, Ronaldo is the current World Player of the Year and has justified his status with 32 goals already this season.
But Rai, the PSG captain, who knows exactly how good a player Ronaldo is, said he was just one of several who could cause the French side problems.

"Ronaldo is an outstanding player and very dangerous not only because of the way he plays but also because he makes so much room and space for the others. We cannot allow him any room and must watch him very closely," he said.

Rai said he had very good memories of playing against Barcelona, having scored both goals against them for Sao Paulo in the World Club Cup final when the Brazilian side beat Barcelona 2-1 in Tokyo in December 1992.
He also scored against them when PSG beat Barcelona 3-2 on aggregate in the European Cup quarter-final in 1994-95.

Seven of the PSG team were in the side that won the Cup Winners Cup last year against Rapid Vienna in Brussels and they are all aware of the apparent jinx that has prevented the holders from retaining the trophy.
Seven previous winners have returned to the final the following season and all have lost. But Ricardo says that fact had not put added pressure on his side.
"I do not think we are the defending champions of this cup anyway," he said. "We are fielding a different team, its a different season."
PSG have had 11 days since their most recent league match on May 3 to prepare for Wednesday's game which could be decided by a golden goal in extra time if the scores are level after 90 minutes.
Barcelona played their last match on Saturday -- a bruising game against Real Madrid -- which they won 1-0 to keep in touch with Real Madrid at the top of the table.

"They are a very good team, a fine attacking team and we know we will be in for a very hard game on Wednesday," said Rai, who added: "We face something of a paradox. We are the Cup holders, but the outsiders to win it again. I think that suits us."
